basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models one delivery of a course or activity to a cohort, not the reusable course definition or curriculum.
Keeps attendance, participation, mastery, completion and credit as distinct assertions.
Binds schedule, modality, location and providers specific to this run.
References assessments, qualifications and credentials held elsewhere.

may: Schedule sessions and allocate rooms or online resources.
Record attendance and participation from approved sources.
Return feedback and progress information to learners.
Report completion status to the learner record master.
mustNot: Infer learning or mastery from login or attendance data alone.
Change grades or completion without authority.
Use learner data for profiling unrelated to the delivery.
Expose learner records to other learners or third parties.
Use proctoring or surveillance beyond what the provider approved.
requiresHuman: Final grading, credit and completion decisions.
Safeguarding concerns involving minors or vulnerable learners.

considerations: Learners, often minors, deserve privacy and protection from surveillance.
Accessible delivery matters for learners with disabilities.
Automated progress judgments can disadvantage some learners unfairly.

items: A delivery has a course reference, a cohort, dates, a modality, instructors and a status.
It is confused with the course definition, an enrollment, a session or a credential.
Learners missing credit due to recording errors.
Safeguarding failures in sessions with minors.
Learner data leaks through learning platforms.
